summary.oneLiner: A 40+ year precision-engineering and industrial tools maker repositioning itself as a Defence & Industrial Powerhouse via 155mm artillery shell manufacturing and a US grease-cartridge acquisition.
summary.business: Sunita Tools Limited manufactures mould bases, ground plates and complex CNC machined precision components, built on a manufacturing foundation of over four decades. Its products serve a wide range of manufacturing industries including automotive, pharmaceuticals, electronics, consumer goods and other engineering sectors. From FY2025-26 the Group extended the same precision machining, large-component manufacturing and process-control competencies into aerospace and defence manufacturing, including 155mm M107 empty artillery shell cases and specialised aerospace components through Group entities and an overseas platform.

Aerospace and defence: Precision machined parts / high-precision machining for aerospace and defence

currentContext.strategies: Build a diversified precision engineering, aerospace and defence manufacturing platform while maintaining focus on quality, customer service, regulatory compliance, capital discipline and execution.|Leverage existing competencies in precision machining, large-component manufacturing, process control and engineering to enter higher-value, technologically demanding aerospace and defence sectors.|Expand precision-manufacturing capacity through advanced CNC and specialised machines, including large machining centres.|Establish manufacturing capability for 155mm M107 empty artillery shell cases, subject to approvals, licences, prototype/product qualification and customer approvals.|Develop specialised aerospace and defence capabilities through Group entities and subsidiaries, pursuing the opportunity via internal capacity creation, customer qualification, strategic relationships and international market development.|Create an international platform - a United States presence through Sunita Defence Inc. (Chicago base) and the acquisition of New Mould Innovations, Kentucky - and continue market development across India, the Middle East, the United States and Europe.|Scout further acquisitions across the globe and pursue selective strategic collaborations where technically, commercially and financially appropriate.|Implement AS9100D in the Vasai CNC machining facility and build an integrated manufacturing ecosystem in which large-format machining, precision engineering and specialised aerospace capabilities complement one another.|Improve conversion of accounting profits into operating cash flows through receivable collections, inventory optimisation, customer payment terms and disciplined working-capital deployment.|Engage Deloitte TTL to review operational, regulatory and statutory compliances.
currentContext.expansion: FY2025-26 was described as a year of investment in manufacturing capacity, specialised machinery, working capital and new business verticals. The Company strengthened its manufacturing infrastructure by adding a few advanced CNC and specialised machines of varying sizes and capabilities, including large machining centres and other precision-manufacturing assets, intended to support both the legacy precision-engineering business and emerging aerospace and defence applications. The flagship expansion is the 155mm M107 empty artillery shell programme: Line 1 at Faridabad has been installed and is designed for approximately 120,000 shells per annum, while Line 2, with an envisaged capacity of approximately 240,000 shells per annum, has been planned with procurement under execution. The Company treats the programme as a capability-development and commercialisation initiative because commercial production and supply remain subject to regulatory approvals, licences, prototype/product qualification and customer approvals. Alongside capacity, the balance sheet expanded through fixed assets and capital work-in-progress, and implementation of AS9100D has been planned at the Vasai CNC machining facility. Internationally, the Group established a United States presence through Sunita Defence Inc. with Chicago as its U.S. base and completed its first U.S. acquisition, New Mould Innovations (NMI), Kentucky, positioned as a manufacturing platform in specialised cartridges and aerospace-grade grease applications, while continuing to scout further acquisitions globally. After year-end the Company announced the addition of two large-size precision machines to support demand in the legacy business, and on 30 July 2026 disclosed an MoU with a Polish defence manufacturer in ISR drones, loitering ammunition and smart flying ammunition, subject to definitive arrangements and regulatory approvals.
currentContext.mdna: The continuing China+1 trend creates opportunities for Indian manufacturers capable of delivering quality, precision, scale and reliable lead times.|India's aerospace and defence manufacturing ecosystem continues to expand, supported by Make in India, Aatmanirbhar Bharat, localisation of defence procurement and growing participation by private-sector manufacturers.|Growth in demand for precision-engineered and large-format components.|Potential commercialisation of artillery-shell manufacturing capacity, subject to approvals and qualification.|International customer development through the Company's U.S., Middle East and European initiatives, aimed at diversifying the customer base and participating in global engineering and manufacturing supply chains.|Greater automation, digital manufacturing, AI-enabled inspection and predictive quality systems.|The aerospace and defence opportunity is accompanied by high entry barriers, including stringent technical qualification, certification, traceability, regulatory approvals and long customer-development cycles.|Post year-end momentum: consolidated net sales value for the quarter ended 30 June 2026 was Rs 18.64 crore compared with Rs 4.14 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous year, representing approximately 350% year-on-year growth.|The Company entered into an interim sales arrangement during FY2025-26 relating to 155mm M107 empty shell cases; commercial production and supply under such arrangements remain subject to regulatory approvals, licences, prototype/product qualification, customer approvals and other contractual conditions.|On 30 July 2026 the Company disclosed a Memorandum of Understanding with a Polish defence manufacturing company engaged in ISR drones, loitering ammunition and smart flying ammunition; the collaboration remains subject to definitive arrangements, regulatory approvals and commercial execution.|The Company has continued to evaluate additional international defence opportunities after year-end; any letter of intent, proposal, tender participation or commercial discussion is subject to due diligence, definitive contracts and regulatory approvals.

risks.risk: Execution risk from rapid capacity expansion into new business verticals
risks.note: Management explicitly flags 'execution risk associated with rapid capacity expansion and new business verticals'. FY2025-26 was a year of simultaneous investment in machinery, working capital, a new artillery-shell line, aerospace subsidiaries and an overseas acquisition - a wide simultaneous build-out for a company of this size.

risks.risk: Dependence on regulatory approvals, licences, product qualification and customer validation for the defence programme
risks.note: Management flags 'delays in regulatory approvals, licences, customer qualification or product validation'. Commercial production and supply of 155mm M107 empty shell cases, including under the interim sales arrangement entered in FY2025-26, remain subject to approvals, licences, prototype/product qualification and customer approvals; the Company itself treats the programme as a capability-development initiative rather than a commercialised business.

Management flags 'working-capital intensity, receivable collection and inventory management'. Operating cash flow remained negative during FY2025-26, reflecting working-capital absorption in receivables, inventory and other operating assets, and management identifies improving the conversion of accounting profits into operating cash flows as an important priority.

risks.risk: Raw-material price volatility and supply-chain disruption
risks.note: Explicitly listed among risks and threats; the business is a metal-intensive precision machining operation whose input costs and delivery lead times depend on material availability.

risks.risk: Foreign-exchange, geopolitical and export-control risk in international markets
risks.note: Explicitly listed among risks and threats. The Group's growth plan rests on the United States, Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Kuwait, the UAE and Europe, and defence products carry export-control and end-user restrictions - the post-year-end Polish defence MoU is itself stated to be subject to regulatory approvals.

risks.risk: Integration and execution risk in subsidiaries and overseas acquisitions
risks.note: Explicitly listed among risks and threats. The Group added aerospace subsidiaries, a U.S. entity (Sunita Defence Inc.) and its first overseas acquisition (New Mould Innovations, Kentucky) while continuing to scout further acquisitions globally.

risks.risk: High entry barriers and long qualification cycles in aerospace and defence
risks.note: Management notes the sector's stringent requirements for licensing, quality, traceability, qualification and regulatory compliance, and that the opportunity carries 'high entry barriers, including stringent technical qualification, certification, traceability, regulatory approvals and long customer-development cycles'. AS9100D implementation at the Vasai CNC facility is still only planned.

risks.risk: Cybersecurity, data protection and intellectual-property risk
risks.note: Explicitly listed among risks and threats; relevant given defence-programme documentation, customer drawings and international technology collaborations.

hero.oneLiner: A 40+ year precision-engineering and industrial tools maker repositioning itself as a Defence & Industrial Powerhouse via 155mm artillery shell manufacturing and a US grease-cartridge acquisition.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- 40+ years in precision engineering with a strong legacy in industrial and capital goods manufacturing, now transforming into a Defence & Industrial Powerhouse.
- Multi-site presence across India (Faridabad defence facility, Ahmedabad, Palghar tools facility) and the US (Sunita Defence Inc. HQ in Chicago; New Mould Innovations in Kentucky).
- Strategy is oriented toward exports and the 'Atmanirbhar Bharat' (self-reliant India) defence manufacturing push.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)
capital_allocation.body: - Capital infusion is directed toward capex for Line 2 and business acquisitions, working capital requirements, and R&D for future business opportunities.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Defence Market] Global defence market estimated at $6.8 billion growing at 8% CAGR (source: Fortune Business Insights); India's defence production reached Rs 1.46 lakh crore in FY25 and is projected to reach Rs 3 lakh crore before FY29, with private-sector share crossing Rs 32,000 crore (~22%) and growing faster (25-40% CAGR) than DPSUs (15-18%).
- [Management] Leadership includes founder-promoter Chairman Sanjay Kumar Pandey, Managing Director Satish Kumar Pandey, Executive Director Tarun Thapar (3+ decades manufacturing artillery shells), CFO Aankit Shah, and family members leading EMEA operations, technology, and US strategic investments via Sunita Defence Inc.
- [Track Record] Listed on the BSE SME platform in October 2023; recognised with 'Best Performer' awards from the Council of International Awards (UK, 2003) and Synergy-Sidel India (2017).
